speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned suffering from a chronic cough and recurrent bronchitis; can you tell me exactly how long you have been experiencing these symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: 51-year-old woman. The patient has been experiencing an aggressive cough producing copious amounts of thick, foamy, yellow-green sputum for about 11 years, with exacerbations similar to the current presentation today. Reports that the cough is worse in the morning and has had multiple evaluations in the past due to recurrent bouts of bronchitis requiring antibiotics treatment. The patient is a non-smoker.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that detailed history. Given the chronic nature of your cough and the specific description of copious, thick, foamy, yellow-green sputum, could you tell me if you have experienced any shortness of breath or wheezing during these exacerbations?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Aggressive cough with thick, yellow-green sputum. I also have Cough worse in the morning, History of recurrent bronchitis.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Bronchiectasis. The combination of an 11-year history of chronic cough, copious purulent sputum, morning predominance, and recurrent "bronchitis" in a non-smoker is highly specific for this condition. I will request a High-Resolution CT (HRCT) of the chest to confirm the diagnosis. REQUEST IMAGES
